<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תמוז_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919577_theRebbe_550" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_9E_D7_95_D7_96_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919577_theRebbe_550__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This very ability to receive nurture through two opposite modes depends on a person's divine service.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Now, this very matter—that they can receive nurture through these two modes—</t>
    <t s="1">depends on the service of man.</t>
    <t s="2">For it is written,</t>
    <t s="3">"Yaakov is the rope of His inheritance."</t>
    <t s="4">As a parable,</t>
    <t s="5">a rope whose one end is tied above and the other end below—</t>
    <t s="6">when the lower end is moved, the upper end also moves.</t>
    <t s="7">And so it is in the service of the souls of Israel,</t>
    <t s="8">that according to the manner of man's service below, so it is made above.</t>
    <t s="9">That is, when a person lowers himself into material things,</t>
    <t s="10">instead of his inner will being for G-dliness in Torah and prayer,</t>
    <t s="11">he lowers himself into material things,</t>
    <t s="12">thereby causing above an increase of tzimtzumim until nurture for the external forces can come from this.</t>
    <t s="13">And likewise, when a person elevates himself in a manner of haughtiness and arrogance,</t>
    <t s="14">even though he knows well his own lowliness,</t>
    <t s="15">nevertheless he elevates himself without reason or knowledge,</t>
    <t s="16">then "spirit brings spirit,"</t>
    <t s="17">causing nurture for the external forces from a very high place.</t>
    <t s="18">And this is the matter of Pharaoh, the letters of "the back of the neck" (HaOref),</t>
    <t s="19">who receives from the aspect of the back of the neck of Arich,</t>
    <t s="20">which is a very high level,</t>
    <t s="21">and this matter depends on service,</t>
    <t s="22">that when "they turned to Me their back and not their face"</t>
    <t s="23">(as stated in the Haftarah),</t>
    <t s="24">then through this the aspect of Pharaoh is drawn, who nurses from the back of the neck of Arich Anpin,</t>
    <t s="25">where "as the darkness, so is the light," etc.</t>
    <t s="26">And this is the matter of the double-edged sword,</t>
    <t s="27">to cut off their nurture from both modes.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>In the detailed explanation, the three ministers of Pharaoh correspond to the throat's structures and their counterparts in holiness.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">D)</t>
    <t s="1">And to understand the matter in detail,</t>
    <t s="2">it is explained in the books of Kabbalah and Chassidus, in the discourses on Egypt and the Exodus from Egypt,</t>
    <t s="3">that Egypt (Mitzrayim) is the straits of the throat,</t>
    <t s="4">for in the throat there are three aspects,</t>
    <t s="5">the windpipe, the esophagus, and the jugular veins,</t>
    <t s="6">which are the three ministers of Pharaoh,</t>
    <t s="7">the chief cupbearer, the chief butcher, and the chief baker.</t>
    <t s="8">And behold,</t>
    <t s="9">just as there is Egypt and the three ministers of Pharaoh in the side of impurity,</t>
    <t s="10">so too there is Egypt and the three ministers in holiness.</t>
    <t s="11">For the chief cupbearer is the drawing down of pleasure,</t>
    <t s="12">since water causes all kinds of pleasure to grow,</t>
    <t s="13">and this is the matter of drawing down the Divine pleasure throughout the entire order of the chain of descent.</t>
    <t s="14">And in the human body, this is the windpipe,</t>
    <t s="15">for in the windpipe there are the nerves of the brain, and through the nerves, pleasure is drawn from the brain throughout the entire body,</t>
    <t s="16">as our sages, of blessed memory, said,</t>
    <t s="17">"There are three windpipes; one branches to the heart, one branches to the lungs, and one branches to the liver,"</t>
    <t s="18">which are the general organs,</t>
    <t s="19">and this is the aspect of the windpipe, which draws pleasure from the brain through the nerves of the brain throughout the entire body.</t>
    <t s="20">And in service, this is the study of Torah with pleasure,</t>
    <t s="21">for pleasure is the inwardness of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="22">and likewise, pleasure in prayer,</t>
    <t s="23">this is the aspect of the chief cupbearer.</t>
    <t s="24">And the chief butcher in service is the matter of the boiling of the blood in holiness,</t>
    <t s="25">which is the aspect of love like flames of fire,</t>
    <t s="26">for the chief cupbearer is the aspect of love with pleasures, which is love drawn like water,</t>
    <t s="27">and the chief butcher is love like flames of fire.</t>
    <t s="28">And the chief baker is Torah,</t>
    <t s="29">and this is so even though it was stated above that the chief cupbearer is Torah,</t>
    <t s="30">for that is the pleasure of Torah,</t>
    <t s="31">but Torah in general is the matter of the chief baker,</t>
    <t s="32">for Torah is called "wheat" (Chitah),</t>
    <t s="33">numerically equivalent to twenty-two,</t>
    <t s="34">the twenty-two letters of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="35">and from the wheat one must make bread,</t>
    <t s="36">as it is written,</t>
    <t s="37">"Come, eat of my bread,"</t>
    <t s="38">and in order for the wheat to become bread, this is through baking,</t>
    <t s="39">as it is written,</t>
    <t s="40">"And ten women shall bake your bread in one oven,"</t>
    <t s="41">where the oven is the heat of love like flames of fire,</t>
    <t s="42">and "one" is the Unique One of the world,</t>
    <t s="43">and "one oven" means the heat and flames of fire in the matter of the Unique One of the world,</t>
    <t s="44">thus there are two matters here,</t>
    <t s="45">the matter of the oven, which is the flames of fire,</t>
    <t s="46">and the matter of the Unique One of the world, which is most sublime,</t>
    <t s="47">and this is the aspect of the chief baker, which is the Torah,</t>
    <t s="48">which is the intermediary between the two lines of the chief cupbearer and the chief butcher.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>These three ministers in holiness cut off the vitality from the three ministers of Pharaoh in the side of impurity.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And these three ministers in holiness cut off the vitality from the three ministers of the side of impurity.</t>
    <t s="1">For behold, also in the side of impurity there are three ministers of Pharaoh,</t>
    <t s="2">the chief cupbearer in the side of impurity is pleasure in material matters,</t>
    <t s="3">for even though it is the desire for that which is permitted,</t>
    <t s="4">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="5">one who is immersed in them causes that he is not at all connected to a G-dly matter.</t>
    <t s="6">And the chief butcher is the boiling of the blood in material things and also in physical things.</t>
    <t s="7">And the chief baker is that his entire matter is not invested in Torah but in physicality.</t>
    <t s="8">And through the three ministers as they are in holiness, they cut off the nurture from the three ministers of Pharaoh of the side of impurity.</t>
    <t s="9">For behold,</t>
    <t s="10">through the chief cupbearer in holiness, which is the service of love with pleasures,</t>
    <t s="11">whose matter is the drawing down of pleasure in the chain of descent through the Sefirah of Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="12">which is the aspect of the windpipe,</t>
    <t s="13">"Acquire wisdom, acquire understanding,"</t>
    <t s="14">behold, through this he cuts off the nurture that they nurse from a high place,</t>
    <t s="15">for when the drawing down is through Chochmah, whose matter is self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="16">then they are unable to receive,</t>
    <t s="17">because,</t>
    <t s="18">what they nurse from the high place,</t>
    <t s="19">this is only when it is in the aspect of the encompassing light specifically,</t>
    <t s="20">but when it is drawn down internally,</t>
    <t s="21">then they are unable to nurse,</t>
    <t s="22">as is explained in Kuntres U'Mayan</t>
    <t s="23">at length.</t>
    <t s="24">And this is the matter of the chief cupbearer, who cuts off the nurture from the high place.</t>
    <t s="25">And through the chief butcher in holiness, he cuts off the nurture from the multitude of tzimtzumim,</t>
    <t s="26">which is caused by a person lowering himself into material things,</t>
    <t s="27">and this is that through the love like flames of fire and the boiling of the blood in holiness,</t>
    <t s="28">the boiling of the blood in the side of impurity is consumed,</t>
    <t s="29">which is what the Targum translates for the verse "chief butcher"</t>
    <t s="30">as "Rav Katulya" (chief slaughterer),</t>
    <t s="31">whose matter is as stated in the Gemara</t>
    <t s="32">on the verse,</t>
    <t s="33">"He who offers a sacrifice of thanksgiving honors Me,"</t>
    <t s="34">"Whoever slaughters his evil inclination," etc.,</t>
    <t s="35">meaning that through the boiling of the blood in holiness, he consumes the boiling of the blood in the side of impurity,</t>
    <t s="36">and consequently the nurture from the aspect of the multitude of tzimtzumim is nullified.</t>
  </section>
